hero.headline: Van Hollen declines to rule out challenging Schumer for Senate Democratic leader as caucus debates strategy
hero.teaser: Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland told reporters Monday that he has not ruled out running against Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader, saying he is in listening mode abou
hero.body:
Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland told reporters Monday that he has not ruled out running against Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader, saying he is in listening mode about a potential bid. Van Hollen said the party should not have a coronation and that he has not shut the door on a challenge to Schumer, who is currently minority leader and widely expected to be elected to lead the new Senate majority in January.

Van Hollen's comments come as some Senate Democrats have withheld support for Schumer while seeking clarity on the party's strategy for the next two years. Democrats are scheduled to meet as a group Tuesday to discuss their path forward. Senator Elissa Slotkin of Michigan, who met with Van Hollen on Monday, said she will not vote for a majority leader candidate who cannot articulate a plan, especially for the first 100 days. Slotkin declined over the weekend to rule out her own leadership ambitions.

Both Van Hollen and Slotkin are viewed as potential presidential contenders. Van Hollen had previously suggested his focus was on 2028 and ensuring Democrats win back the White House.

Schumer needs only a majority of the Democratic caucus to win the leadership election during a closed-door meeting scheduled for early December. Many Senate Democrats have expressed support for Schumer following the party's performance in last week's midterm elections. Senator Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut said Monday he plans to continue supporting Schumer but added that the Senate needs new ideas, energy from incoming members, and changes in how it operates.

cards.body:
Nine tanker planes were relocated from RAF Mildenhall following a separate security incident at another British base.

military moved nine refueling aircraft from Royal Air Force Base Mildenhall in England to bases in Germany and Spain on Monday amid a reported threat from Iran, according to The Wall Street Journal. Four planes went to Spangdahlem Air Base in Germany, one to Ramstein Air Base in Germany, and four to Morón Air Base in Spain.

cards.teaser: France has formally accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of orchestrating cyberattacks that sabotaged supermarket refrigeration systems across France and Europe last mo
cards.body:
France has formally accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of orchestrating cyberattacks that sabotaged supermarket refrigeration systems across France and Europe last mo

Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot announced that France had summoned the Iranian ambassador to Paris and said the government would impose sanctions on those responsible. Iran has not officially responded, though some Iranian media outlets have dismissed the allegations as baseless.

cards.headline: Israel's new parliament sworn in as Eisenkot seeks to form government and unseat Netanyahu
cards.teaser: Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has 28 days to build a coalition after receiving backing from 67 lawmakers, but neither his bloc nor Netanyahu's won a majority in last month's election.
cards.body:
Israel's new parliament was sworn in Tuesday as opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot seeks to form a government and oust caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. President Isaac Herzog tasked Eisenkot, a former army chief, with building a coalition after he received backing from 67 members of the 120-seat Knesset, compared to 46 for Netanyahu. Eisenkot has 28 days to assemble a majority, with a possible two-week extension.

Eisenkot's bloc won 48 seats in last month's election while Netanyahu's won 53, leaving both short of a majority. Arab-led parties won a record 19 seats and could prove decisive, though Netanyahu ruled out governing with them and some of Eisenkot's potential partners oppose including them in a coalition. Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister until a new government forms.

cards.headline: Nvidia shares drop 4 percent, wiping $250 billion off market value, after board launches probe into CEO affair
cards.teaser: Nvidia stock fell sharply Monday after the board announced an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's admitted affair with Alice Huang, whom U.S. officials believe was a Chinese intelligence operative.
cards.body:
Nvidia stock fell sharply Monday after the board announced an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's admitted affair with Alice Huang, whom U.S. officials believe was a Chinese intelligence operative.

Nvidia shares fell approximately 4 percent by close of trading Monday, erasing about $250 billion in market value, following the company's announcement that its board would conduct an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The board action came after Huang admitted in a company message that he had an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip company Megaspeed, whom U.S.

cards.headline: National average gas price falls below $4 per gallon for first time since July
cards.teaser: Oil prices plunged 13% last week as President Trump signaled he would not strike Iran and Democrats gained control of Congress in midterm elections.
cards.body:
The nationwide average price for regular gasoline fell below $4 per gallon Tuesday for the first time since July 20, according to motor club AAA. The average dropped to $3.97 from $4.14 on Election Day, while diesel prices fell to $6.15 from $6.28.

The decline follows a 13 percent plunge in oil futures last week after President Donald Trump told NBC News he did not plan to attack Iran. Oil prices slid further after Democrats won control of the House and Senate in Tuesday's midterm elections, with markets betting that Congressional oversight would constrain the Iran war that Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu launched February 28.

hero.headline: Krakow mass shooting suspect dies in hospital as Polish prosecutors say motive investigation continues
hero.teaser: The gunman suspected of killing six people in central Krakow and three family members at their home died in a hospital early Monday morning, Polish police said. The 24-year-old Pol
hero.body:
The gunman suspected of killing six people in central Krakow and three family members at their home died in a hospital early Monday morning, Polish police said. The 24-year-old Polish man was shot by police officers within three minutes of opening fire in the city's Main Market Square on Saturday afternoon. He had been hospitalized with injuries sustained during a gunfight with responding officers.

Polish prosecutors said Monday that investigations into the suspect's motive remain ongoing, walking back earlier statements by a government minister who described the gunman as inspired by far-right ideologies and ultra-nationalism. Przemysław Nowak, a spokesperson for Poland's National Prosecutor's Office, told reporters the motive inquiry continues. The suspect has not been officially named.

The attack killed four Polish citizens, a British national, and an Austrian woman in the Main Market Square. Police later found three bodies at the gunman's home, identified as his 53-year-old father, 52-year-old mother, and 21-year-old sister. Authorities seized four firearms from the suspect's car, including two AR-15 rifles and two handguns, along with several hundred rounds of ammunition. Polish media reported the suspect held a firearms permit.

Sixteen people were hospitalized after the shooting, including two police officers who were injured during the gunfight with the suspect. A surgeon who was eating nearby when the attack began rushed to the scene and helped treat victims before ambulances arrived. Professor Michał Pędziwiatr said his colleague used his hand to stem bleeding from a severely injured police officer, and that intervention undoubtedly saved the officer's life. Both wounded officers have since emerged from comas.

Poland declared two days of national mourning following the attack. Prime Minister Donald Tusk visited Krakow and said the country had not previously experienced such drastic terrorism.

cards.headline: Israeli forces kill 14-year-old Palestinian boy in West Bank raid
cards.teaser: Palestinian health ministry says Moataz Daghlas was shot dead during military operation in village near Nablus.
cards.body:
Israeli forces shot and killed 14-year-old Moataz Daghlas during a military operation in the West Bank village of Burqa, northwest of Nablus, according to the Palestinian health ministry. The Israeli military said soldiers identified people who intended to throw stones and fired to remove the threat. Two others were wounded, including a 17-year-old shot in the abdomen and pelvis.

According to the United Nations, at least 98 Palestinians, including 22 children, have been killed by Israeli forces or settlers in the West Bank since the start of the year. The UN Human Rights Office said it verified 241 Palestinian children killed by Israeli security forces and settlers in the West Bank since October 2023, finding none posed an imminent threat to life when killed.

cards.headline: Police officer killed in backpack explosion in northern Spain
cards.teaser: An explosive device detonated as officers investigated a shooting scene in Oviedo, leaving one dead and another seriously injured.
cards.body:
A police officer died and another was seriously injured after an explosive device hidden in a backpack detonated in Oviedo, Spain. Officers responded to reports of a dispute between neighbors and found a woman with gunshot wounds. While searching for the suspect, they discovered a suspicious backpack with a flashing light and contacted bomb disposal and canine units.

The explosion occurred as officers moved the package outside to protect residents. A police dog was also killed in the blast. The suspect fled the scene and remains at large. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said he was deeply shocked by the incident and praised the injured officer's dedication and courage.

hero.headline: ICE detains 8-year-old Haitian boy at routine check-in after TPS termination, prompting San Diego school district response
hero.teaser: Immigration and Customs Enforcement detained an 8-year-old Haitian boy at a routine appointment in downtown San Diego last week, separating him from his uncle and transferring him
hero.body:
Immigration and Customs Enforcement detained an 8-year-old Haitian boy at a routine appointment in downtown San Diego last week, separating him from his uncle and transferring him to federal custody, according to school officials and an advocacy group. The boy, a third grader at Fay Elementary School, lost his Temporary Protected Status protections this summer after a Supreme Court decision allowed President Donald Trump to end TPS for Haitians. He was summoned to meet with ICE officers Wednesday, and his uncle brought him to the appointment to comply with the law, according to a letter San Diego Unified School District officials sent Friday to the Department of Homeland Security and the Department of Health and Human Services.

ICE officers determined the boy to be an unaccompanied minor after the uncle could not establish legal guardianship, according to a DHS spokesperson. The agency said it removed the boy from the household out of caution to ensure his safety. The boy was subsequently transferred to the Office of Refugee Resettlement, which takes custody of children deemed unaccompanied minors. As of Monday, his family did not know where he was being held, according to Representative Juan Vargas.

The boy had been living with his uncle and cousins after his father was deported last year, according to the school district and the Haitian Bridge Alliance, an immigrant rights advocacy group. TPS is a humanitarian designation that had shielded hundreds of thousands of Haitians from deportation following the country's 2010 earthquake. The protections were renewed multiple times as Haiti descended into crisis, with gangs now controlling much of the capital after the president was assassinated in 2021.

The school district said it is sending crisis counselors to Fay Elementary School this week because the boy's classmates have expressed concern and fear for him. School officials asked DHS and HHS to reconsider how immigration enforcement policies are affecting students, but as of Monday had received no response. The Office of Refugee Resettlement said it does not comment on specific cases. The boy is among 1,640 children considered unaccompanied minors currently in HHS care.

A Wisconsin state trooper originally from South Africa was released from federal custody late Friday after being detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement officials at an air

Carel Aaron Van Der Merwe was released under an order of supervision following intervention by Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, according to his attorney. Van Der Merwe entered the United States in 2019 at age 14 and attended high school in New Mexico, according to attorney Mark Christopher.

cards.headline: Six killed in shooting in Krakow, Poland; British citizen among dead
cards.teaser: A gunman killed six people and injured more than a dozen others in a shooting in central Krakow, Poland, on Saturday afternoon, authorities said. A British citizen was among the fo

A gunman killed six people and injured more than a dozen others in a shooting in central Krakow, Poland, on Saturday afternoon, authorities said. A British citizen was among the fo

A British citizen was among the four women and two men killed when the attacker drove onto Main Market Square, a popular tourist attraction in Poland's second-largest city, and began firing at people. Three of the dead were Polish and two have not been identified.

cards.teaser: Authorities arrested a 20-year-old man in connection with a shooting that killed one person and injured another during homecoming weekend at Winston-Salem State University in North
cards.body:
Authorities arrested a 20-year-old man in connection with a shooting that killed one person and injured another during homecoming weekend at Winston-Salem State University in North

Ziyaire Antonyo Spinks faces charges of murder, assault with a deadly weapon with intent to kill inflicting serious injury, and felony possession of a firearm on an educational campus, Winston-Salem Police Department said Sunday. The shooting Saturday night killed Peyton Izaia Patterson, 19, and injured Alyssa Janae Ellerbee, 19, who was treated at a hospital and released.

cards.headline: Secret Service arrests man near White House with guns who said voices told him to kill Trump
cards.teaser: The Secret Service arrested a man Thursday night near the White House after officers found him in a parked vehicle with multiple guns and ammunition and he told them he heard voice
cards.body:
The Secret Service arrested a man Thursday night near the White House after officers found him in a parked vehicle with multiple guns and ammunition and he told them he heard voice

Officers approached Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos after observing him acting suspiciously in a parked car, according to a Department of Homeland Security statement. Chrinos described hearing voices instructing him to come to Washington and kill the president, the statement said.

hero.headline: Anthropic sets $70-78 IPO price range, targeting up to $1.4 trillion valuation in largest-ever tech offering
hero.body:
Anthropic, the startup behind the Claude AI assistant, on Tuesday set an initial public offering price range of $70 to $78 per share, positioning what could become the largest IPO in history. At the midpoint, the company would raise $61 billion and achieve a valuation of roughly $1.1 trillion when combined with options and unvested stock. At the top of the range, Anthropic could be valued at $1.4 trillion. The company plans to begin trading as soon as next week.

The five-year-old company has experienced rapid revenue growth, recording $33.2 billion in sales in the first nine months of this year compared to $4.6 billion for all of 2025. Sales in the most recent quarter reached $17 billion, up 1,127% from the same period a year earlier. However, Anthropic has had only one quarter of operating profit and faces nearly $900 billion in committed spending on computer power and data center infrastructure over the next few years. The company acknowledged in its prospectus that such growth rates are not sustainable and it cannot guarantee revenue will continue to grow.

Investor concerns center on customer concentration and the company's unusual structure. Five customers accounted for a quarter of Anthropic's sales this year, with some of those customers also being competitors potentially building their own AI models. The company has implemented a complex share lock-up schedule that permits some non-founder insiders to sell 10% of their holdings immediately, with 23 additional dates over the first year when employees can sell more shares. The seven founders retain majority voting power through a special ownership structure.

The offering comes amid challenging market conditions for AI companies. Last week, AI-linked stocks declined on concerns about data center development, and Nvidia shares fell 5% on Monday following CEO Jensen Huang's admission of an affair and announcement of a foreign intelligence investigation. The Wall Street Journal reported that Anthropic has scheduled meetings with key investors this week and plans to list shares Thursday or Friday next week.

cards.headline: SoftBank posts $7 billion quarterly loss on U.S. AI data center power costs, Intel decline
cards.teaser: The Japanese investment giant recorded losses tied to power generation equipment procurement for U.S. data centers and falling Intel shares, though its OpenAI stake showed $45 billion in cumulative gains.
cards.body:
SoftBank Group reported a fiscal second-quarter net loss of 1.12 trillion yen ($7 billion) on Tuesday, driven by a 597.2 billion yen ($3.7 billion) loss from changes in procurement plans for power generation equipment for U.S. AI data center projects and declining Intel share values. The company made advance investments totaling $9.48 billion to secure power equipment amid supply concerns and long lead times.

SoftBank's Vision Fund segment swung to a loss of 81.58 billion yen from a 2.38 trillion yen profit a year earlier. The company's cumulative investment in OpenAI stood at $54.6 billion with a fair value of $99.6 billion and cumulative gains of $45 billion as of September 30.

cards.teaser: President confirms investigation into Jensen Huang after affair wiped $250 billion off company's market value

President confirms investigation into Jensen Huang after affair wiped $250 billion off company's market value

President Donald Trump said the Federal Bureau of Investigation is investigating the relationship between Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang and an alleged Chinese spy. Trump told reporters he spoke with Huang on Monday and believes the CEO did not know the woman was a spy.

cards.headline: Rocket Lab shares fall over 8% as Neutron delays overshadow record revenue and backlog growth
cards.teaser: The space company reported record quarterly revenue and $1.2 billion backlog growth but investors focused on launch timeline concerns.
cards.body:
Rocket Lab shares dropped more than 8% despite the company reporting record third-quarter revenue and a 52% sequential increase in its backlog to $1.2 billion. The space company also posted positive operating cash flow and secured over $515 million in Neutron launch contracts from constellation operators during the quarter.

Investors focused on delays to the Neutron rocket launch timeline, which overshadowed the financial results. The company guided to record revenue and gross margin expansion in the fourth quarter.

cards.headline: Skims offers refunds on $148 advent calendar after social media criticism
cards.teaser: Kim Kardashian's company is refunding customers after the accessories calendar was mocked for items like hair clips and keychains.
cards.body:
Skims is offering full refunds for its $148 advent calendar after widespread social media criticism of the product's contents. The accessories calendar promised twelve days of surprises but was mocked online for items including hair clips, hair ties, and keychains that critics compared to items found in a sofa.

A company spokesperson said that for some customers the calendar did not meet expectations and that Skims has personally contacted every purchaser to offer a full refund or store credit. The shapewear and clothing company, co-founded by Kim Kardashian in 2019, was valued at $5 billion in 2025.

cards.headline: Qantas to outsource 850 jobs to Accenture, most moving to India
cards.teaser: Qantas will outsource 850 corporate jobs to consulting firm Accenture, with most of the positions moving to India, as the Australian airline accelerates investment in artificial in
cards.body:
Qantas will outsource 850 corporate jobs to consulting firm Accenture, with most of the positions moving to India, as the Australian airline accelerates investment in artificial in

Chief Executive Vanessa Hudson announced the plan in an internal email to staff on Tuesday, saying the job cuts will begin in mid-2027. The outsourcing will start with finance, procurement, human resources, and marketing roles shifting mostly to teams in India and some to Australia.

hero.headline: Google DeepMind uses AI to formally verify Signal protocol cryptography
hero.body:
Google DeepMind researchers used agentic artificial intelligence to mathematically prove a number of the Signal protocol's key cryptographic guarantees, marking a development for both the widely used encryption standard and AI-assisted formal verification. The researchers completed the project in four weeks using a new AI framework called AlphaProof Code, according to a report published Tuesday.

The analysis serves as independent validation of the cryptography that protects communications on platforms including the Signal app, Google Messages, and WhatsApp. The DeepMind analysis did not find any new vulnerabilities in the portions of the Signal protocol it examined. When researchers tested AlphaProof Code on older versions of Signal containing known and previously fixed vulnerabilities, the system correctly identified them and showed that those versions could not be formally verified. The researchers are releasing the specification and proof they developed to aid other formal verification work.

Formal verification uses mathematics to validate that software functions as intended without critical vulnerabilities. Before AI assistance, the process was time-consuming, requiring people to describe software characteristics, convert them into formulas, and develop proofs. Agentic AI can significantly reduce the time required for this work. The DeepMind analysis was limited in scope and did not formally verify the entire Signal mobile app. The researchers were able to accelerate their work partly because the Signal Foundation has conducted some past formal verification work on smaller portions of the code.

"While prior formal verification focused on smaller portions of the code, Google DeepMind's approach enables significant expansion," Ehren Kret, Signal's chief technology officer, said in a statement. DeepMind researchers say they developed a human-AI collaboration process that allows AI agents to contribute and self-correct at almost every phase while seeking human input and review at key points. The researchers emphasized their findings represent one milestone in a larger process, and questions remain about whether AI-automated formal verification can scale across the technology sector at a workable cost. Google declined to share the cost of the analysis or comment on plans for a commercial formal verification product.

cards.headline: Google patches eighth actively exploited Chrome zero-day of 2026
cards.teaser: Users of Chrome and Chromium-based browsers urged to update immediately as Google addresses latest security vulnerability.
cards.body:
Google issued a security update for Chrome to patch the eighth actively exploited zero-day vulnerability discovered in 2026. The company is withholding technical details until most users install the fix and any affected third-party libraries are patched.

Users should update Chrome to version 157.0.8103.50 or .51 for Windows and macOS, and 157.0.8103.50 for Linux. Users of Chromium-based browsers including Microsoft Edge, Brave, Opera, and Vivaldi should apply patches when available. Google has now addressed eight actively exploited Chrome zero-days since January.

cards.headline: Hugging Face exec warns cyberattacks could force open AI platforms to close access
cards.teaser: Recent breaches at OpenCode and Fireworks highlight vulnerabilities that may push industry toward restrictions on contributors and features.
cards.body:
Irene Solaiman, chief policy officer at Hugging Face, warned that escalating cyberattacks on open AI platforms could force the industry to restrict access to contributors and features. Recent incidents include an October attack on OpenCode that compromised users' third-party API keys and a breach at AI infrastructure startup Fireworks on Monday that exposed some customers' model weights, datasets, and billing information.

Solaiman said stricter measures could include identity verification requirements and contributor vetting, potentially excluding independent researchers and hobbyists. Hugging Face has increased credential rotation frequency and network controls rather than limiting participation. She cautioned that expensive monitoring tools may not be affordable for all platforms, creating a risk that open source systems could close down despite growing industry and government support for open AI models.

cards.headline: Ukraine's fiber-optic drone production squeezed by AI data center demand
cards.teaser: Global AI infrastructure buildout is straining optical fiber supply, driving up costs for Ukrainian manufacturers who already face disadvantages against Russian imports from China.
cards.body:
Global AI infrastructure buildout is straining optical fiber supply, driving up costs for Ukrainian manufacturers who already face disadvantages against Russian imports from China.

Ukrainian drone manufacturers are facing higher costs and tighter supplies of fiber-optic cable as global demand from artificial intelligence data centers competes for the same material used in unjammable battlefield drones. The market research firm TrendForce expects a worldwide fiber shortfall of 111 million miles in 2026.

cards.headline: Otter.ai adds 27 languages, including mid-meeting language switching
cards.teaser: The AI note-taking platform will support 31 languages total and can automatically transcribe conversations as speakers change languages without manual adjustments.
cards.body:
Otter.ai announced Tuesday it is adding support for 27 languages and launching a feature that automatically follows conversations as speakers switch languages during meetings. The expansion brings the platform's total language support to 31, with transcription continuing seamlessly when a conversation moves between languages such as English, Korean, and Portuguese without requiring users to adjust settings.

Thirteen languages are available now, including Mandarin Chinese, Korean, German, Italian, Portuguese, and Russian. The remaining 14, including Arabic, Hindi, Swedish, and Hebrew, are coming soon. The update follows Otter's $320 million funding from General Catalyst and recent workplace features including meeting preparation tools and real-time coaching.

cards.headline: Valve adds average FPS data to Steam Deck game store pages, plans desktop PC expansion
cards.teaser: The feature displays performance statistics collected from players who opted in to share anonymous framerate information.
cards.body:
Valve has introduced average framerate statistics for Steam Deck games directly on Steam store pages, covering thousands of titles including those rated Verified, Playable, and Unsupported. The data comes from players who agreed to share anonymous performance information and appears under Steam Deck Compatibility sections, with histograms showing how frequently different framerates occur.

Valve is testing expansion of the feature to desktop PCs, prompting Steam Client Beta users to opt in to anonymous framerate reporting. The company has not announced when desktop performance statistics will become available. Unlike Steam Deck systems with standardized framerate limits, desktop PCs use varying hardware configurations that will require additional information to present comparable results.

cards.headline: Nintendo updates Switch consoles to prepare for eShop game gifting
cards.teaser: The feature will allow family group members to send digital games and content to each other starting November 17.
cards.body:
Nintendo released firmware version 23.5.0 for Switch and Switch 2 consoles to support an upcoming eShop feature allowing Nintendo Account family group members to gift digital games to one another. The gifting capability, scheduled to launch November 17, will enable users to send games, downloadable content, and upgrade packs to members within their family group of up to eight people.

Supervised accounts cannot send gifts, and Nintendo has placed limits on the number of gift purchases allowed within a given period. The company previously offered a more expansive gifting system on the Wii that allowed users to send games to anyone on their friend list, but that ended when the Wii Shop Channel closed in 2019.

hero.headline: Bills join 49ers atop NFL at 7-1 as season reaches midpoint
hero.body:
The Buffalo Bills moved to 7-1 on Monday with a 23-6 victory over the Minnesota Vikings, joining the San Francisco 49ers at the top of the NFL standings as the regular season reached its halfway point. The Bills defense limited Minnesota quarterback Carson Wentz to eight completions on 25 attempts before he was benched in the fourth quarter. The Vikings dropped to 6-2 and fell from first to third in the NFC North, where all four teams now have at least six wins.

The Denver Broncos set a new NFL record on Sunday by extending their streak of regular-season wins in one-score games to 16 consecutive victories. Denver scored two touchdowns in the fourth quarter and sacked Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young in the final minutes to secure a 26-21 road win. The victory was the Broncos' fifth straight and moved them to 7-2 atop the AFC West heading into their bye week.

The Cincinnati Bengals improved to 6-2 with a 34-17 victory over the Atlanta Falcons at Madrid's Bernabeu Stadium in the seventh of nine international games this season. Quarterback Joe Burrow completed 24 of 29 passes for 271 yards and was involved in four touchdowns, while wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase recorded a season-high 155 receiving yards. The Bengals scored more than 30 points for a fourth consecutive game, tying a team record, and moved into a tie atop the AFC North with the Pittsburgh Steelers at 6-2.

The Chicago Bears also reached 7-2 after Cairo Santos made a 38-yard field goal as time expired to beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 27-24. The victory was Chicago's fourth straight win and moved them into second place in the NFC North. The 49ers, who defeated the Las Vegas Raiders 38-17, remain 7-1.

cards.headline: Clarke calls for reopening of 2018 ball-tampering investigation after Khawaja claims entire team knew
cards.teaser: Former Australia captain says fans "can't trust what's real" following new allegations about the sandpaper scandal
cards.body:
Former Australia captain says fans "can't trust what's real" following new allegations about the sandpaper scandal

Former Australia captain Michael Clarke has called for the investigation into the 2018 ball-tampering scandal to be reopened after Usman Khawaja claimed the entire team knew about the use of sandpaper during the third Test against South Africa. Clarke told 2DayFM that Australian fans "can't trust what's real" and need the truth to emerge, arguing the investigation process should be restaged despite Cricket Australia CEO Todd Greenberg stating he sees no compelling reason to reopen the case.

cards.headline: Arsene Wenger considers FIFA presidential run against Gianni Infantino
cards.teaser: The former Arsenal manager is weighing a challenge to the embattled FIFA president ahead of the November 18 candidacy deadline.
cards.body:
Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger is considering running against Gianni Infantino in FIFA's presidential election, according to BBC Sport. Senior European football figures have been urging the 77-year-old to enter the race, and he is now giving it serious thought. Wenger would have UEFA's backing as it leads opposition to Infantino, whose standing weakened after a failed plan to sell commercial stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

The candidacy deadline is November 18, with the election scheduled for March. Infantino retains support in South America, Africa, and Asia and recently claimed backing from the "vast, vast majority" of world football. Wenger, FIFA's head of global development, distanced himself from Infantino's abandoned commercial proposal but has not yet decided whether to run.

cards.headline: McIlroy says DeChambeau running out of options after LIV collapse
cards.teaser: Rory McIlroy comments on Bryson DeChambeau's uncertain future following LIV Golf's collapse, as McIlroy pursues a record-tying eighth Race to Dubai title.
cards.body:
Rory McIlroy said Bryson DeChambeau is running out of competitive options following the collapse of LIV Golf, though adding the two-time U.S. Open champion to the DP World Tour would bring more attention to the circuit. DeChambeau can apply for DP World Tour membership based on his major championship status, which would offer a path to regain his PGA Tour card for 2028.

McIlroy was speaking in Dubai before the DP World Tour Championship, where he chases a record-equaling eighth season-long title. The Northern Irishman trails Spain's Eugenio Chacarra by 533 points in the Race to Dubai standings but would guarantee his fifth straight crown with a victory this week at Jumeirah Golf Estates.

cards.headline: UFC 334 features Ciryl Gane's first heavyweight title defense and Amanda Nunes' return
cards.teaser: Ciryl Gane defends his heavyweight title against Josh Hokit, while former champion Amanda Nunes challenges Kayla Harrison for the bantamweight belt at Madison Square Garden.
cards.body:
Ciryl Gane will make his first defense of the UFC heavyweight title against Josh Hokit at UFC 334 in New York on Saturday. The Frenchman was promoted to undisputed champion in September after Tom Aspinall vacated the belt due to complications from an eye injury. Gane is the betting favorite against Hokit, who has won all four fights since joining the UFC last November.

The co-main event features Amanda Nunes returning from retirement to challenge Kayla Harrison for the bantamweight title. Nunes, widely considered the greatest female MMA fighter in history, last competed in 2023 before retiring. Harrison is making her first title defense after winning the belt from Julianna Pena last year.

cards.headline: BBC opens voting for Women's Footballer of the Year with five-player shortlist
cards.teaser: Voting is now open for the BBC World Service Women's Footballer of the Year 2026, with the winner to be announced at Sports Personality of the Year in December.
cards.body:
The BBC World Service has opened worldwide voting for its Women's Footballer of the Year 2026 award. The five-player shortlist includes Temwa Chawinga, Ewa Pajor, Alexia Putellas, Alessia Russo, and Khadija Shaw. Voting closes November 18 at 9:00 a.m. GMT.

For the first time in the award's 12-year history, the winner will be announced during the BBC's Sports Personality of the Year on December 13. The award covers the period from September 2025 through August 2026, with contenders nominated by coaches, journalists, and former professionals.

cards.headline: Dortmund fans' group criticizes Nmecha goal celebration
cards.teaser: A supporters' group objects to the midfielder's gesture, saying it references a campaign with positions against homosexuality and transgender identity.
cards.body:
A Borussia Dortmund supporters' group criticized midfielder Felix Nmecha's goal celebration during Saturday's 2-1 win over Elversberg, saying it referenced a campaign by Christian organization Ballers in God called 'The King's Return.' The group said the campaign discriminates against homosexuality and transgender people, paints abortion as "Satan's plan," and conflicts with Dortmund's values of tolerance and diversity.

Nmecha, who pointed to the sky and mimed removing a crown after scoring twice, said there were "misunderstandings" and that his celebration was "not intended to promote myself or any organisation." Ballers in God, founded by former Premier League midfielder John Bostock, said it seeks to "demonstrate love and respect towards everyone" and that its focus is "to point people to Jesus with grace and love."

hero.headline: M. John Harrison becomes oldest Booker Prize winner at 81 for post-apocalyptic novel The End of Everything
hero.body:
M. John Harrison has become the oldest ever winner of the Booker Prize, receiving the prestigious literary award for his post-apocalyptic novel The End of Everything. Harrison, 81, was named the winner of the £50,000 prize at a ceremony in London on Monday, surpassing Margaret Atwood as the oldest recipient in the award's history.

The End of Everything is set in the years after a mysterious catastrophe that caused British society to collapse. The story follows a man and his aunt navigating life on the south-east English coast in the aftermath of an unexplained disaster and the arrival of mysterious alien beings. Harrison has said he deliberately omitted explanations about the background events to make readers feel the same disorientation as the characters, calling it a disaster story in which the disaster is the failure to comprehend.

Dame Mary Beard, who chaired the Booker judges, said the book turns readers upside down and surprisingly leaves them with a twinge of optimism given the subject matter. Booker Prize chief executive Gaby Wood described Harrison as the first Booker winner to have emerged from the science fiction world, calling The End of Everything a realist book about a strange world populated by desperate, unmoored characters. The book has divided readers, with critics variously describing it as baffling, brilliant, and tender and terrifying in equal parts.

Harrison, who has built a cult following over his 60-year career, began writing in the 1960s and has published 13 novels, five short story collections, and what he calls an anti-memoir. He told BBC Radio 4 on Tuesday that he wanted to write a book satirizing the present-day barrage of information without the necessary tools to understand it. The Booker Prize judges reached a unanimous decision after what Dame Mary described as a day of discussion, disagreement, and debate over six shortlisted novels.

cards.headline: David Walliams accused of grooming fans as young as 15 after losing injunction bid
cards.teaser: The Guardian published allegations after the former Britain's Got Talent judge failed to block the story in court.
cards.body:
David Walliams has been accused by The Guardian of grooming fans he met when they were as young as 15 and harassing women in the workplace over several years. The comedian and former Britain's Got Talent judge denies the allegations. The Guardian and ITN published the story after Walliams failed to obtain a High Court injunction blocking it.

Walliams left Britain's Got Talent in 2022 after allegations he made sexually explicit comments about contestants. Publisher HarperCollins ended his contract in 2025 following an internal investigation into alleged inappropriate behavior toward junior female staff and stopped selling his books earlier this year.

cards.headline: David Walliams named in sexual misconduct allegations after failed injunction
cards.teaser: The comedian was identified after a judge refused his request to keep his name secret. He denies wrongdoing.
cards.body:
David Walliams has been publicly identified as the celebrity facing sexual misconduct allegations after losing a legal bid to conceal his identity. A London High Court judge dismissed his injunction request against The Guardian and ITV News on November 3, ruling he could be named. Multiple women have accused the 55-year-old comedian and children's book author of using his status to groom them for sex, with allegations spanning decades.

Walliams denied wrongdoing in a statement, saying he never abused power and is not a sexual predator. He acknowledged behaving thoughtlessly in past casual relationships and said he is devastated some women now express hurt. HarperCollins dropped Walliams and his catalog last year following an internal investigation into inappropriate behavior toward young female employees.

cards.headline: Jemima Goldsmith says she was victim of Russell Brand's violence and coercive control
cards.teaser: The producer revealed she once called police to remove Brand from her home during a violent incident, speaking out after his rape conviction.
cards.body:
Jemima Goldsmith has said she was a victim of Russell Brand's "violence, coercive control and abuse" during their relationship over a decade ago. The producer and writer revealed she once called police to remove Brand from her house during a violent incident but chose not to press charges at the time out of concern for her teenage sons.

Goldsmith spoke out days after Brand was convicted last week of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault and sentenced to more than 10 years in prison. She said she had been assisting journalists in exposing Brand's behavior and expressed relief that he "has finally faced justice."

cards.headline: Producer Jemima Goldsmith accuses Russell Brand of violence during 2013-14 relationship
cards.teaser: Goldsmith alleged Brand was abusive and required police removal from her home in 2014, following his conviction and sentencing for rape and sexual assault.
cards.body:
Producer Jemima Goldsmith publicly accused Russell Brand of violence, coercive control, and abuse during their 2013-14 relationship, following his conviction and sentencing to more than 10 years in prison for rape and sexual assault. Goldsmith said she called police to remove Brand from her home during a violent incident in 2014 but chose not to press charges, citing concern for her teenage children.

Goldsmith revealed she assisted Channel 4, The Times of London, and The Sunday Times with their 2023 reporting on Brand and offered to testify in court if the outlets faced a lawsuit. She said the published allegations influenced women to pursue criminal proceedings against Brand, leading to his conviction last week.

cards.headline: Jennifer Hudson to headline Vatican's Concert With the Poor in December
cards.teaser: The EGOT winner will perform at the seventh annual event, attended by Pope Leo and thousands, including over 3,000 people experiencing poverty.
cards.body:
Jennifer Hudson will headline the Vatican's Concert With the Poor on December 5 in the Holy See's Paul VI Hall, with Pope Leo scheduled to attend. The seventh annual event will be performed before roughly 8,000 participants, including over 3,000 people in conditions of poverty and vulnerability who will receive a hot takeaway dinner afterward.

The EGOT-winning singer and actress will be accompanied by the Rome-based Nova Opera Orchestra and the choir of the Diocese of Rome. The event will be broadcast live on Italian television and streamed worldwide by major Catholic broadcasters. Hudson previously performed at the Vatican in September 2025 during the Grace for the World concert in St. Peter's Square.

cards.headline: Phil Rosenthal's 'Somebody Feed Phil' moves to YouTube with United Airlines sponsorship
cards.teaser: The food travelogue show departs Netflix after eight seasons, with United Airlines as title sponsor for season nine on YouTube.
cards.body:
Phil Rosenthal's food and travel series "Somebody Feed Phil" is moving to YouTube from Netflix, where it streamed for eight seasons. United Airlines will serve as title sponsor for the ninth season and offer the show on its seatback entertainment systems.

United will provide production support with crew and equipment, according to Rosenthal, creator of "Everybody Loves Raymond." The airline is offering MileagePlus members a chance to win flights and a meal with Rosenthal by guessing which cities will appear in season nine. United hopes the sponsorship will inspire travelers to visit destinations on its routes, says chief advertising officer Maggie Schmerin.

hero.headline: Seven Republican senators call for delay in GOP leadership elections
hero.teaser: Seven Republican senators are calling for the Senate GOP leadership elections to be delayed, with one threatening to skip the vote if the postponement does not occur. The elections
hero.body:
Seven Republican senators are calling for the Senate GOP leadership elections to be delayed, with one threatening to skip the vote if the postponement does not occur. The elections are scheduled for Tuesday, and Senate Majority Leader John Thune of South Dakota is still expected to be reelected to lead the Senate GOP.

Senators Ron Johnson of Wisconsin, Rick Scott of Florida, Mike Lee of Utah, Ted Budd of North Carolina, and John Kennedy of Louisiana signed a letter demanding the elections be delayed to allow more discussion about the party's performance last week. Senators Dave McCormick of Pennsylvania and Jim Banks of Indiana supported the effort in statements posted on social media. Johnson threatened to skip the vote if the delay does not happen.

The decision on whether to delay falls to conference chair Tom Cotton of Arkansas, though such decisions are usually made with leadership input. The election is expected to proceed as planned Tuesday morning unless a senator motions to delay and the motion passes with a majority, which appears unlikely given the limited number of public supporters, according to a source familiar with the planning discussions. Despite arguments that Thune should not secure his leadership position so quickly, no one has announced a challenge to him.

None of the leadership elections are competitive. Senate Majority Whip John Barrasso of Wyoming, Conference Chair Tom Cotton of Arkansas, Policy Committee Chair Shelley Moore Capito of West Virginia, and Conference Vice Chair James Lankford of Oklahoma are expected to retain their positions.

cards.headline: Democrats will control both chambers of Congress in 2027 but lack veto-proof majorities
cards.teaser: President Trump has signaled he will use his veto power liberally to block Democratic legislation, forcing potential compromise.
cards.body:
Democrats have secured 54 Senate seats and 254 House seats for the incoming Congress, according to Associated Press projections, with several races still uncalled. Neither majority reaches the two-thirds threshold needed to override a presidential veto without Republican support.

President Donald Trump has publicly signaled he will use his veto power frequently, posting an image of a hat reading "VETO" as election results arrived and displaying a similar hat on the Resolute Desk during a signing ceremony. Trump told Fox News that Democrats could send him "50 different great bills" but he would "send them back with a nice stamp, veto."

cards.headline: Democrats win state elections as voters approve tougher sentencing, bail limits
cards.teaser: Democrats gained at least 12 state legislative chambers and won five governorships while voters approved all six statewide ballot measures tracked proposing stricter criminal penalties.
cards.body:
Democrats gained at least 12 state legislative chambers and won governorships in Georgia, Iowa, Nevada, Ohio and Texas in last week's elections. Voters simultaneously approved all six statewide ballot measures tracked by Ballotpedia that proposed tougher sentences, criminal penalties or bail restrictions in 2026, including five that passed on November 3 in Indiana, Louisiana, Tennessee and Colorado.

Some Democratic winners adopted tougher border security language while opposing former President Trump's immigration policies. Texas Senator-elect James Talarico called himself a border security Democrat and criticized former President Biden for failing to secure the border. Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed said days before the election that tougher border security was needed while also criticizing Trump's use of immigration enforcement.

cards.headline: State Department objects to El Salvador's Haiti military operations despite Trump's support
cards.teaser: Diplomatic notes show career officials raised concerns about coordination, while Trump told President Bukele to "do what you have to do."
cards.body:
State Department officials have objected to El Salvador's military operations against gangs in Haiti, even as President Trump gave his full support to the effort, according to diplomatic notes. After Salvadoran special forces launched operations in Port-au-Prince following Trump's October 27 blessing, U.S. Chargé d'Affaires David Howell complained to Haiti's prime minister that El Salvador was not coordinating with international forces and urged a halt to operations.

El Salvador issued a formal rebuke Monday, calling Howell's claims about Salvadoran casualties and misdirected fire false and questioning his credibility. The dispute exposes friction between Trump's foreign policy objectives and career diplomats, with one U.S. official saying some bureaucrats oppose the president's goals for the Western Hemisphere.

cards.headline: Van Hollen declines to rule out challenging Schumer for Senate Democratic leader as caucus debates strategy
cards.teaser: Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland told reporters Monday that he has not ruled out running against Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader, saying he is in listening mode abou
cards.body:
Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland told reporters Monday that he has not ruled out running against Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader, saying he is in listening mode abou

Van Hollen said the party should not have a coronation and that he has not shut the door on a challenge to Schumer, who is currently minority leader and widely expected to be elected to lead the new Senate majority in January. Van Hollen's comments come as some Senate Democrats have withheld support for Schumer while seeking clarity on the party's strategy for the next two years.

Senators Ron Johnson of Wisconsin, Rick Scott of Florida, Mike Lee of Utah, Ted Budd of North Carolina, and John Kennedy of Louisiana signed a letter demanding the elections be delayed to allow more discussion about the party's performance last week.

cards.headline: DeSantis positions for 2028 presidential run as Rubio deflects speculation following GOP midterm losses
cards.teaser: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis is positioning himself for a 2028 presidential campaign while Secretary of State Marco Rubio has dismissed reports he is considering a White House bid
cards.body:
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis is positioning himself for a 2028 presidential campaign while Secretary of State Marco Rubio has dismissed reports he is considering a White House bid

The maneuvering by both Florida Republicans underscores volatility in the early stages of the 2028 primary, where Vice President Vance had been viewed as a likely frontrunner before Tuesday's election results. DeSantis, whose term as governor ends in January, has fueled speculation through a postelection media campaign that included appearances on podcasts and CNN.
